I'm not fond of this separation between hidden and exposed, especially in the first version.

Please, clarify.

I guess that in Compact it would be better to require that the off-circuit have an exact in-circuit analog. 
That is, do not allow the mismatch (but computationally binding match) between the two that we sometimes perform.

Is this worth mentioning?
Would this be a limitation?

It feels that some of the applications of "recursion" will require this, e.g. a proof aggregator.
I'm not sure how we are gonna do this with Compact.
The `transcript_repr` of the vk is not enough. We also need include all the vk commitments (maybe hashing them with the `transcript_repr`) just like in our multi circuit aggregator.
We are gonna have a circular dependency. Currently `aggregation` depends on `zk-stdlib`.
It is currently not available as part of the midnight stack. In this document I'm explaining how users will be able to use this feature.
Why?

```suggestion
Currently, compact does not support **in-circuit proof verification ([MPS 14](https://github.com/midnightntwrk/midnight-improvement-proposals/blob/main/mps/mps-0014-proof-verification-recursion.md)).**
Multi-step off-chain computations therefore cannot be expressed as a single
```
This is being discussed in the `mindight-zk` section, not in the compact. Do you think that the compact behaviour will be different between IVC chains and PCD?
I think the only way to abstract this from the ledger would be by introducing the new logic in the `verify` function and `MidnightVK`. We'll figure out a way to resolve this circular dependency.

IMO, this match between off-circuit and in-circuit is related to the IVC functionality that we expose in midnight-zk, rather than compact. The compact side will only need to worry about the public inputs (which might be the state), but should not worry about how that state is represented (or what it represents) off-circuit.

```suggestion
A verifying key is uniquely represented in-circuit by the hash of its `transcript_repr` 
together with the commitment to all its fixed columns. This is the canonical handle 
for reasoning about VKs inside a Compact circuit.
```

> during execution

We need to be very clear *which* part of execution this occurs during. I _strongly_ believe this should occur at transaction validation time, not during contract execution, to preserve the existing architectural split between validation and state modification.
It's going to be a bit confusing talking about this – what is the 'state' from Compact's perspective? It's unlikely to be the contract state itself; is it the Impact transcript?
Agreed with Inigo, I'd focus on exposing the most general primitive we can here, we can worry about how Compact uses it later.
It's not clear to me how these relate to the prior section on IVC. Are these used to build IVC? Do they use IVC internally?
I think in compact-lingo, `vk` and `public_inputs` would need to be `disclose`d for use in `verifyProofExposed`.
Given that `verifyProofHidden` seems strictly more powerful than `verifyProofExposed` we need to articulate the additional cost well.

This is a bit thin. Ideally we'd have a formal format spec. But I also think we're missing a discussion of what to do with different versions of the verifier key format, and if we have interop between them.

The state will be defined outside of compact, and is something that belongs to to the IVC chain, not necessarily the compact smart contract. Once we send the IVC proof to compact, it will be sent alongside its state to be validated, and it is only then that compact will do something with it. 

The recursive state could be the contract state itself, or part of it. Take for example a rollup. The state could be a merkle tree of UTXOs. Off-chain you use an IVC chain to update the state with valid transactions. When you move back to compact, you can update that field of its state (the tree root) together with the proof.

This section tries to be generic - compact will have functionality to verify any proof generated with `midnight-zk`. These proofs could be IVC chain proofs generated using `midnight-zk`, but they could be any other proof.  In this first deliverable, compact will not be involved in building IVC - only in verifying proofs.
👍  I'll add a formal format spec, and also a comment on what happens when VK formats change.
The two variants are described in terms of a cost/privacy trade-off, but neither is anchored to a specific MPS-0014 UC.
I'm removing the hidden function.
